newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MCGRATH PUTS AUSTRALIA ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCGRATH PUTS AUSTRALIA ON TOP.

text.p: Australian paceman Glenn McGrath confirmed his status as the world's leading bowler with a devastating new ball burst on the first day of the first test at the Wanderers.
South Africa reached lunch on 58 for three after McGrath had exploited ideal seam bowling conditions to pick up three wickets for 10 runs in a brilliant spell of 10 overs.
The first came off the fourth ball of the innings when Andrew Hudson offered a leaden footed push outside off stump and was caught behind for a duck.

In McGrath's fifth over Jacques Kallis, on six, steered a full length ball into the safe hands of Mark Waugh at second slip and the home side were 25 for three in the 15th over when Gary Kirsten offered a second catch behind to Ian Healy, pulling wildly at a short ball to be out for nine.

Leg spinner Shane Warne was then introduced as first change to greet Daryll Cullinan. Warne, Cullinan's bete noir when the two sides met in 1993, had his man dropped at short leg by Matthew Hayden when he had scored 18. At lunch Cullinan had reached 19 with Hansie Cronje on 21.
As expected Australia left out Andrew Bichel and went into the match with just two specialist seamers in McGrath and Jason Gillespie. South Africa omitted Adam Bacher from their squad.
